analysis.title: GOAL Kickstart: Below zero – Risk Appetite Indicator negative as Tech dominates cross-asset moves
key_insights: GS cross-asset Risk Appetite Indicator (RAI) fell to -0.5, its lowest since April 2025. Readings below -1 and near -2 have historically been useful contrarian signals. The current level is not yet negative enough to send that signal, but it implies less-constrained upside for risky assets than at the end of summer.
Credit components drove most of the RAI decline and weighed on the PC1 'Global growth' factor. The bond yield rally supported the PC2 'Monetary policy' factor.

Tech has become a larger driver of risk appetite. The correlation between the RAI and Nasdaq 100 performance relative to the S&P 500 equal weight has risen over recent years and reached almost 1 in recent weeks.

Differences in sensitivity to semiconductor stocks explain cross-asset performance over the past 3 weeks, more so than sensitivity to oil prices. The Dollar has also behaved in a more pro-cyclical fashion.
Credit excess returns saw another multi-standard-deviation sell-off last week. G4 10y bonds rallied, giving some protection against the AI sell-off.

Most Euro Area-exposed assets underperformed their betas to global growth and monetary policy pricing as OAT-Bund spreads widened beyond fundamentals. Euro Area flash PMIs declined below expectations, while US PMIs were roughly unchanged.
Within equities, defensive/quality styles and Value outperformed their growth- and policy-implied returns, which buffered broad equity markets against the Tech-driven momentum unwind.

Options markets price more uncertainty over the next 2 weeks than the following 4 weeks, consistent with a busy catalyst calendar. Nasdaq 100 and other equity indices price larger moves this week (Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon report). Long-dated USTs and HY credit price larger moves next week around the US mid-term elections.
GS economists expect a Fed hold this week followed by a hike in December. The BoJ and ECB also meet this week.

GOAL asset allocation stays modestly pro-risk: OW Equities (3m/12m), UW Credit (3m/12m), OW Cash (3m), OW Bonds (12m). GS thinks earnings support, lighter positioning and lower valuations should help equities into year-end, despite AI concerns, Middle East tensions and mid-term elections.

GS forecasts S&P 500 at 8,000 (3m), 8,300 (6m) and 8,700 (12m) from 7,624. Brent is forecast at $88 (3m), $83 (6m) and $75 (12m) from $117, and gold at $4,715 (3m), $4,850 (6m) and $5,235 (12m) from $3,996.
Commodities over the past week: S&P GSCI +1.4% (energy +3.3%, precious metals -4.2%, agriculture -2.6%). Over 1 year the GSCI is +62.4% and energy +131.8%.

Valuation: S&P 500 12m forward P/E is 18.6x versus a 10y average of 19.2x (47th percentile). MXAPJ and MSCI EM sit at 0th percentile of 10y valuation range. US 10y yield at 5.0% is in the 99th percentile of the last 10 years.

tension_points.bull_case: Earnings support, lighter positioning and lower valuations should help equities into year-end. The RAI at -0.5 implies less-constrained upside than at end of summer, and readings below -1 to -2 have been contrarian buy signals.
tension_points.bear_case: AI concerns, Middle East tensions and mid-term elections could sustain near-term volatility. Credit sold off by multiple standard deviations and the Tech-driven momentum unwind continues.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A deeper RAI decline toward -1 to -2 would turn the signal contrarian-bullish rather than invalidate the view. The report names no explicit invalidation level.
